basic_information.name: Flowise
basic_information.creator: FlowiseAI (co-founded by Henry Heng and Chung Yau Ong; Y Combinator S23 batch; acquired by Workday in August 2025)
basic_information.description: Flowise is an open-source, low-code platform for visually building AI agents and LLM workflows using a drag-and-drop interface. Built on top of LangChain, it enables users to create chatbots, RAG-driven assistants, single-agent and multi-agent systems, and complex workflow orchestrations without writing extensive code. For entrepreneurs, Flowise is significant because it dramatically lowers the barrier to deploying production-grade AI applications: a small team can self-host the platform on modest hardware (8GB RAM), connect their own LLM API keys, and go from idea to working chatbot or AI workflow in minutes rather than weeks. Since its acquisition by Workday in August 2025, the open-source community edition remains freely available under the Apache 2.0 license, while enterprise features like SSO, RBAC, and audit logs are offered through paid plans.
basic_information.release_date: May 2023 (initial launch); actively maintained with commits as recent as February 2026

technical_capabilities.underlying_models: Multi-provider support for 100+ LLMs, embeddings, and vector databases. Supported chat models include OpenAI (GPT-4o, GPT-4, GPT-3.5), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), Mistral AI, Groq, Azure OpenAI, and any model accessible via LangChain integrations. Also supports local/open-source models via Ollama, HuggingFace, and custom endpoints. Users bring their own API keys.
technical_capabilities.customization_depth: workflow-builder and code-extension. The visual drag-and-drop canvas lets users wire together LLM chains, agents, tools, and data sources. For deeper customization, users can write custom JavaScript functions inside nodes, create custom tools, build custom components, and extend the platform via its API. Supports branching, looping, routing logic, and conditional flows.
technical_capabilities.input_types: Text, images (with vision-capable models), audio (speech-to-text via microphone), PDF, DOCX, CSV, Excel, PowerPoint, JSON, TXT, URLs, web scraping (Playwright, Firecrawl, Apify), Google Drive, S3 files, Notion pages
technical_capabilities.output_types: Chatbot (embeddable widget), API endpoint, text responses, structured data. Workflows produce conversational AI assistants, RAG pipelines, automated content generation, and agent-driven task completions. Outputs are consumed via API, embedded chat widget, or integrated into external systems via webhooks.
technical_capabilities.api_access: Yes. Full REST API for creating predictions, managing chatflows, and interacting with deployed agents. SDKs and code snippets available in Python, JavaScript, and shell. API keys can be configured for authentication.
technical_capabilities.deployment_options: Self-hosted (npm/npx, Docker, Docker Compose), cloud-hosted (Flowise Cloud), and deployable on AWS, Azure, GCP, Digital Ocean, Alibaba Cloud, Railway, Render, HuggingFace Spaces, Elestio, Sealos, RepoCloud. Supports on-premise and air-gapped environments for enterprise. Docker image available at hub.docker.com/r/flowiseai/flowise. Runs on Node.js with minimal 8GB RAM requirement.
technical_capabilities.ai_model_flexibility: bring-your-own-model. Fully multi-provider: users can connect any LLM provider by supplying API keys. Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Groq, Azure, HuggingFace, Ollama, and custom endpoints. No vendor lock-in on the model layer.

user_experience.target_user: developer, business_user, enterprise_team. Primary audience is developers and technical business users who want to prototype and deploy LLM applications without writing boilerplate code. Also targets enterprise teams needing governed AI agent deployment with RBAC and audit trails.
user_experience.learning_curve: hours. Basic chatbot can be built in minutes using templates. More complex multi-agent workflows and RAG pipelines require a few hours to understand the node-based paradigm. Some technical understanding of LLM concepts (API keys, embeddings, vector stores) is helpful but not strictly required for simple use cases.
user_experience.setup_time: 5-15 minutes. Self-hosted via npx (npx flowise start) takes under 5 minutes. Docker deployment takes 10-15 minutes including configuration. Flowise Cloud signup provides instant access.
user_experience.collaboration_features: Workspaces for logical team grouping with separate trust boundaries. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with granular permissions per resource. User invitation system with email, workspace assignment, and role selection. Account admin dashboard for managing users, roles, and workspaces. Enterprise tier adds SSO/SAML, LDAP integration, versioning, and audit logs. Multi-user support and advanced collaboration features are gated behind Cloud and Enterprise plans.
user_experience.template_library: Built-in Marketplace tab with pre-built templates for common use cases including CSV Q&A, PDF chat, Slack bots, conversational agents with memory, retrieval QA chains, and more. Templates are ready-to-use: clicking 'Use Template' creates a new canvas with the same flow, requiring only API key configuration. Community members can contribute templates by exporting chatflows as JSON and adding them to the marketplace. Also integrates with n8n workflow templates for extended automation patterns.
user_experience.visual_builder_type: drag-drop. Three builder modules: (1) Chatflow - basic LLM chain builder, (2) Assistant - beginner-friendly chat assistant creator with RAG and tool calling, (3) Agentflow - the most comprehensive builder supporting single-agent, multi-agent systems, and complex workflow orchestration with branching, looping, and routing logic.

ai_and_rag_capabilities.rag_support: Comprehensive built-in RAG pipeline support. Features include: document loaders for diverse file types (PDF, DOCX, CSV, web pages, Google Drive, S3, Notion), text splitters (recursive, character, token-based), multiple embedding models (OpenAI, HuggingFace, Cohere, custom), and extensive vector store integrations (Pinecone, Chroma, Postgres/pgvector, Weaviate, AstraDB, Qdrant, Milvus, Supabase). Supports advanced techniques like Graph RAG, Agentic RAG (self-improving document QA with iterative refinement), reranker components, and retriever customization. Document Stores feature for managing indexed knowledge bases.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.agent_capabilities: multi-agent and autonomous. Supports single-step tool-calling agents, multi-step conversational agents, multi-agent systems with supervisor-worker patterns, and autonomous workflows. Agent types include OpenAI Tool Agent, Conversational Agent, AutoGPT-style agents, and custom agent configurations. Agentflow V2 enables complex orchestrations with human-in-the-loop checkpoints, execution tracing, and state-aware agent coordination. Supports review checkpoints where human operators validate agent outputs for quality control.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.model_selection: Multi-vendor BYOM (bring your own model). Users freely choose and switch between any supported LLM provider at the node level. Each node in a workflow can use a different model. Supports 100+ models across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Groq, Azure, HuggingFace, Ollama, and custom API endpoints.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.prompt_management: Built-in prompt template nodes with variable injection. Users can define system prompts, few-shot examples, and dynamic prompt templates within the visual builder. Prompt chaining is natively supported. No dedicated prompt versioning system in the community edition, though enterprise plans include versioning features.

integration_and_ecosystem.key_integrations: LLM Providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Groq, Azure, Ollama, HuggingFace), Vector Databases (Pinecone, Chroma, Postgres/pgvector, Weaviate, AstraDB, Qdrant, Milvus, Supabase), Document Sources (Google Drive, Notion, S3, Confluence, web scrapers via Playwright/Firecrawl/Apify), Communication (Slack via custom tools and MCP, Discord, Telegram), Databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB), Automation Platforms (n8n, Zapier, Pipedream for extended workflow automation), Observability (Langfuse, LangSmith for tracing)
integration_and_ecosystem.integration_count: 100+ components including LLMs, embeddings, vector stores, document loaders, tools, and memory modules. Exact integration count is not formally published as a single number, but the platform offers extensive coverage across the LangChain ecosystem plus custom tool creation.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_support: Yes. Flowise natively supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) for connecting AI agents to external data sources and tools. Users can connect to any MCP server (Stdio transport for local, SSE for cloud). Built-in MCP tool nodes and Custom MCP support allow connecting to community MCP servers. Third-party MCP servers also exist (e.g., mcp-flowise Python package) enabling external systems to interact with Flowise chatflows via MCP.
integration_and_ecosystem.webhook_support: Yes. Flowise supports webhooks as URLs that receive HTTP requests with JSON body containing chat messages. Workflows can be triggered via webhook/API calls. Integration with platforms like Pipedream and n8n extends webhook capabilities for complex automation scenarios.
integration_and_ecosystem.export_formats: Embeddable chat widget (JavaScript/HTML), API endpoint (REST), chatflow export as JSON (for sharing/backup/marketplace), code snippets in Python/JavaScript/shell for API consumption. The embed widget is customizable (colors, avatars, messages) and can be deployed as popup or full-page chat. No standalone app export — the platform itself serves as the runtime.

pricing_and_accessibility.pricing_model: open-source (self-hosted is free) with freemium cloud offering. The open-source community edition under Apache 2.0 is completely free to self-host. Flowise Cloud offers tiered subscription plans. Users pay for their own infrastructure and LLM API usage when self-hosting.
pricing_and_accessibility.free_tier_limits: Self-hosted: unlimited, no restrictions on flows, predictions, or features in the community edition. Flowise Cloud Free Plan: $0/month, limited to 2 flows and 100 predictions per month.
pricing_and_accessibility.paid_plans: Flowise Cloud Starter: $35/month (unlimited flows, 10,000 predictions/month). Flowise Cloud Pro: $65/month (unlimited flows, 50,000 predictions/month). Enterprise: custom pricing (on-premise deployment, air-gapped environments, SSO/SAML, LDAP/RBAC, versioning, audit logs, dedicated support). Third-party hosting on Railway starts at $5/month, Sliplane from 9 EUR/month.
pricing_and_accessibility.open_source: Yes. Apache License Version 2.0 for the Community Edition. The repository contains both Community Edition (Apache 2.0, fully open) and Enterprise Edition code. Community edition allows free use, modification, packaging, and distribution including for commercial purposes.
pricing_and_accessibility.self_hosting_option: Yes, and it is straightforward. Three methods: (1) npx flowise start (quickest, single command), (2) Docker / Docker Compose (recommended for production), (3) Clone and build from source. Runs on Node.js, requires approximately 8GB RAM. Extensive documentation for deployment on AWS, Azure, GCP, Digital Ocean, Railway, and other platforms.
pricing_and_accessibility.data_residency_and_sovereignty: Self-hosted deployment provides full data sovereignty — all data stays on your infrastructure, enabling GDPR compliance by hosting within the EU. Flowise Cloud stores data in US East 1 region; international transfers use Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs). For EU organizations, self-hosting on EU infrastructure is the recommended approach for data residency compliance. Enterprise on-premise deployment supports air-gapped environments for maximum data isolation. No specific EU AI Act certification mentioned, but self-hosting model inherently supports compliance requirements.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in the open-source low-code LLM application builder category. One of the top 3 platforms alongside Dify and Langflow. Flowise differentiates through its focus on rapid chatbot/agent prototyping, strong self-hosting story, and accessible visual interface. The Workday acquisition (August 2025) elevated it from community-driven project to enterprise-backed platform, positioning it uniquely at the intersection of open-source accessibility and enterprise governance.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Fortune 500 enterprises including Thermo Fisher Scientific (130,000 employees), Deloitte (450,000 employees), Accenture (750,000 employees), and AWS. UneeQ uses Flowise for their embedded analytics platform and AI brain (Synapse). Industries span consulting, finance, healthcare, customer service, and scientific instrumentation. Post-acquisition, Workday's 10,000+ enterprise customers gain access to Flowise capabilities.
adoption_and_market.community_size: 47,200+ GitHub stars and 23,300+ forks (as of February 2026). Active open-source community with regular contributions. Millions of conversations and workflows processed. Y Combinator S23 batch alumni. Active Discord community. npm package available (flowise). Docker Hub image actively maintained.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Y Combinator S23 batch (standard YC investment of $500K for 7% equity). No publicly disclosed seed or Series A rounds prior to acquisition. Acquired by Workday (NASDAQ: WDAY, ~$70B market cap) on August 14, 2025, for undisclosed terms. The acquisition validates the platform's enterprise value and ensures long-term development resources.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: (1) Dify — production-ready AI apps, higher GitHub stars (~58K), broader app-building focus; (2) Langflow — RAG-specialized, acquired by DataStax, 23% faster on complex RAG benchmarks; (3) n8n — general automation + AI, fair-code model, stronger in workflow automation beyond AI; (4) Voiceflow — conversational AI focused, more enterprise-ready out of box; (5) Stack AI — no-code AI builder targeting enterprise. Flowise differentiates through Apache 2.0 licensing, lightweight self-hosting, visual simplicity, and now Workday enterprise backing.
adoption_and_market.ecosystem_lock_in_risk: low. Apache 2.0 open-source license allows full code access, modification, and redistribution. Chatflows exportable as JSON. No proprietary data formats. Multi-provider model support prevents LLM vendor lock-in. Self-hosting eliminates platform dependency. However, complex workflows built in Flowise's visual format are not directly portable to competing platforms — migration would require rebuilding flows. Post-Workday acquisition, the open-source community edition remains available but future feature parity with enterprise edition is uncertain.

teaching_and_classroom.class_project_idea:
Project 1 — 'Build a Startup FAQ Chatbot' (60 min): Students create a customer support chatbot for a fictional startup. They upload a PDF business plan or FAQ document, configure a RAG pipeline with an embedding model and vector store (in-memory for simplicity), connect it to an LLM (GPT-4o-mini via free-tier API key), and deploy an embeddable chat widget. Students test the chatbot with real customer questions and iterate on the system prompt to improve response quality. Deliverable: a working embedded chatbot URL and a 5-minute pitch on how this reduces customer support costs for their startup.

Project 2 — 'Multi-Tool AI Agent for Market Research' (90 min): Students build an AI agent that can search the web (via SerpAPI tool), query a product database (via custom tool), and summarize findings. They configure a multi-step agent flow with tool selection logic, test it with market research queries for their startup idea, and present the agent's output alongside their analysis of when AI agents add value versus manual research. This demonstrates agentic AI concepts from Session 5 while reinforcing business decision-making.

Official tutorials page: https://docs.flowiseai.com/tutorials (RAG, agents, tools, MCP). Official video tutorials: https://docs.flowiseai.com/using-flowise/agentflowv1/sequential-agents/video-tutorials. Codecademy tutorial: https://www.codecademy.com/article/flowise-ai-tutorial (step-by-step no-code agent building). DataCamp tutorial with demo project: https://www.datacamp.com/tutorial/flowise. teaching_and_classroom.student_prerequisites: basic prompting. Students should understand what LLMs are and have experience with basic prompting (e.g., ChatGPT usage). No coding required for basic projects, though understanding API keys and basic JSON structure is helpful for advanced configurations. Familiarity with the concept of RAG (retrieving documents to augment AI responses) is beneficial but can be taught during the session.
teaching_and_classroom.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt engineering & no-code tools): Primary fit — hands-on chatbot building with visual drag-and-drop, RAG pipeline creation, prompt template configuration. Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects): Secondary fit — demonstrates Build vs Buy decisions (self-hosted Flowise vs. cloud AI services), CRISP-DM data preparation via document loaders. Session 5 (Ethics, governance & final presentations): Tertiary fit — human-in-the-loop checkpoints, data sovereignty via self-hosting for GDPR compliance discussion.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Ideal for: (1) Early-stage startups (pre-seed to seed) that need to prototype AI-powered features without hiring an ML team — a single technical co-founder can build and deploy chatbots, RAG assistants, or AI agents in days. (2) Teams of 1-5 people who want to self-host for cost control and data privacy. (3) B2B SaaS startups adding conversational AI or document intelligence features to their product. (4) Startups in regulated industries (health, finance, legal) where self-hosting ensures data sovereignty. (5) AI agencies building custom chatbot solutions for clients — Flowise provides a reusable platform across projects. Less ideal for: consumer-facing apps needing pixel-perfect UI (Flowise produces functional but basic chat widgets), or teams with zero technical members (some understanding of APIs and LLM concepts needed).
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_mvp: Hours to days. A basic RAG chatbot MVP can be built in 1-2 hours using templates. A more sophisticated multi-agent workflow with custom tools takes 2-5 days. Full deployment with Docker, custom domain, and production configuration takes about 1 week. The visual builder dramatically accelerates iteration — changing models, prompts, or data sources is as simple as rewiring nodes, versus rewriting code in traditional development.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Flowise when: (1) You need full control over your AI stack and data (self-hosting), (2) Your use case fits the chatbot/agent/RAG paradigm, (3) You want to avoid per-message cloud pricing at scale, (4) You need to iterate quickly on LLM workflows without coding. Consider building custom when: (1) You need highly specialized ML pipelines beyond LLM chains, (2) Your application requires custom UI beyond chat widgets, (3) You need sub-100ms latency for real-time applications. Consider buying (e.g., Voiceflow, Botpress) when: (1) You need enterprise-grade conversation design tools, (2) Your team has zero technical capacity, (3) You need managed hosting with SLA guarantees. Cost comparison: self-hosted Flowise on a $20/month VPS + LLM API costs vs. $65/month Flowise Cloud vs. $500+/month for enterprise alternatives.
entrepreneurial_relevance.key_lessons: 1. Self-hosting is a superpower for startups: Flowise on a $5-20/month server gives you unlimited AI workflows — the only variable cost is LLM API usage, making unit economics predictable and scalable. 2. Visual prototyping accelerates product-market fit: drag-and-drop workflow building lets non-ML founders test AI product hypotheses in hours, not weeks — fail fast, iterate faster. 3. Open-source does not mean unsupported: with 47K+ GitHub stars, Y Combinator backing, and Workday acquisition, Flowise demonstrates that open-source projects can achieve enterprise credibility and long-term sustainability. 4. Data sovereignty is a competitive advantage: in the EU context (GDPR, AI Act), being able to self-host your AI infrastructure on European servers is a selling point for B2B startups targeting enterprise clients. 5. The LLM layer is commoditized — the workflow layer is the moat: Flowise shows that value increasingly lies not in which model you use, but in how you orchestrate models, data, and tools into useful workflows — entrepreneurs should focus on the orchestration and domain expertise, not the underlying models.
